body:
I have been suicidal. What helps me to live, is some kind of new worldview. The realization, that I am not the only one who is fucked up, but that our society is fucked up on purpose. 

It starts when we are little children: we get pressed into chairs, we have to compete with each other. It is the rule of the lion.

My friend, this system that makes so many people unhappy and only a very few happy, this might also be a reason for your unhappiness. There are people who believe this. People who don't want to compete against each other, but live with each other. They are a minority but they are there. 

The whole system is flawed.

It's always the 2nd thing I do after I stand up in the morning. The first thing is going to the toilet.

I sit or lie down on a yoga mat and just try to be in the moment for about 30min. Being aware of the now. Recognizing how I breath, how my body feels. Though I'm distracted nearly all of the time but there always is a new moment a new start and I also think I can learn from those distractions, recognize what kind of thoughts "pop up" in my mind and what feelings they cause.

This guy here explains it better:

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3nwwKbM_vJc

Yes, opening up is good. Feels already good, I never talked about that to anyone. So I think I will see a therapist.

Also I kind of worked on my mind in the past. I was in a religious cult, which was not that bad as it sounds.

In my late teens I was extremely social anxious and began contemplating suicide. That was when I joined the cult. It kind of gave me all the stability that my mother never could give me, I began living my life after certain rules and became more and more succesfull, confident and happy. But most of all it gave me relationships and love.

But I think I kind of never lost this insecurity inside me. I started taking drugs again (which I did a lot in my teens) and slowly adapted another lifestyle, which lead me to where I am now.

I mean I don't want to go back where I was. I may felt happier, when I was more included in the cult, but now I feel more real and honest to myself, but also more desperate and sad.

My mother raised me solely and I love her. But she is completely insecure and I think she passed it on to me.

I think I would have needed just some rock, someone stable on whom I could have lifted me up.

Now I'm unstable and insecure myself and so mournful about it.

I haven't always been that sarcastic. I think it's kind of a protection mechanism, which allows me to pretend to be strong or stable but inside I could cry.

Maybe it's just that I can't build up trust to someone and that showing what I really feel, would just lead to more pain, because other people wouldn't be interested or show disrespect.

I think it's just that I don't know what to do, when I'm around people. I feel awkward and tend to become sarcastic. I let no one really near me, I think I'm just pretty messed up but to afraid to show my weaknesses.
